1.6.1 High voltage
DANGER
The MODULITH SLX-F2 operates with high voltages to generate shock-
waves. When working on high voltage circuits or on components that
are electrically in contact with high voltages, personnel must observe the
following to avoid injury:

[Doc: SM SLX-F2(25k) 0516.pdf | Page: 27]
following to avoid injury:
Switch off the MODULITH SLX-F2 and wait 10 minutes before starting
any work on the HV circuit. This time is required to discharge the capaci-
tors in the PCCU completely.
Use the grounding rod to ground all components that could possibly
carry high voltage before performing any work on the PCCU.
This applies to the following parts and assemblies:

[Doc: SM SLX-F2(25k) 0516.pdf | Page: 27]
This applies to the following parts and assemblies:
– Pulse current charging unit (PCCU)
– High voltage cable from PCCU to therapy head
– Therapy head with coil

WARNING

sure.
Hydraulic oil may spurt out under high pressure when parts of the hy-
draulic unit are damaged or opened for service. Hydraulic oil may cause
injuries.
Before starting any service operation on the hydraulic unit switch off the

The mechanical function of the in-line unit is determined by the interaction of linear springs, a rotational

ear springs try to push the transducer upwards, while the rotational spring in the spring-pulley tries to pull

the transducer downwards via the toothed belt. The force of the linear springs is always bigger than that
of the rotational spring. In between the springs, the motor is coupled to the toothed belt via a driving-

body or the mechanical limit) only the difference between the force of the linear springs and that of the

Driving the transducer downwards:
The transducer is pulled downwards by the motor via the toothed belt. Hereby the three linear springs are
